entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Cool and quantitative - a measured shortfall below the amount or degree required, with none of the verdict *wanting* carries.

entries.definition: lacking the requisite qualities or resources to meet a task
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The flat general word for falling short of what a task demands, registering the shortfall without turning it on whoever bears it.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Puts the unmet requirement down to capacity - not that the standard was missed but that it could not be reached.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The harshest here, reading a missed requirement as a verdict on fitness rather than a measurement of it.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The plainest of these, naming the missing amount outright and stopping there.

entries.definition: inadequate in number of workers or assistants etc.
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Informal, and it carries the strain of working a job with too few hands rather than the bare count.
examples: they're rather short-handed at the moment

entries.definition: inadequate in number of workers or assistants etc.
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: States the shortfall as a plain condition of the staff on hand, neither excusing it nor blaming anyone for it.

entries.definition: inadequate in number of workers or assistants etc.
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Measures the people present against the strength the work was meant to have, framing the gap as a post held by too few.

entries.definition: inadequate in number of workers or assistants etc.
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The flattest of the four - a headcount below requirement, without the felt pressure of *short-handed*.

entries.definition: lacking the requisite qualities or resources to meet a task
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Weighs what is brought against what the task takes and finds the two mismatched, where *inadequate* names the shortfall as a defect in the thing itself.
examples: she was unequal to the task

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The gentlest way of saying the requirement went unmet, setting the demand beside the resource and leaving the failure unassigned where *incompetent* pins it.
examples: unequal to the demands put upon him

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Formal and weighted, as though the amount had been tested against a standard and pronounced short, where *lacking* only reports the gap.

entries.definition: expressing yourself easily or characterized by clear expressive language
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Plain approval of clear, easy expression - it credits a speaker with getting the thought out whole, without *eloquent*'s claim on beauty.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The strongest praise in the family - expression so ready and effective that the manner of it is admired alongside the matter.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: A cool compliment: it names the effortlessness of the speaking and stops there, where *eloquent* reaches for admiration.
examples: able to dazzle with his facile tongue

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Praise for speech that runs without a catch in it - flow, where *eloquent* claims power.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The figure spelled out at full length, praise with a flourish that plain *fluent* never attempts.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Figurative and frankly ornamental - it admires the sound of the speaking, where *articulate* admires only its clarity.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Approving of the delivery itself - words that arrive without friction - and plainer in register than *eloquent*.

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The bare fact of having speech at all, carrying none of the approval that *articulate* does.

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Purely descriptive and formal: it records the capacity to speak and passes no verdict on how well.

entries.definition: speaking or spoken fittingly or pleasingly
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Approves speech that fits the occasion and pleases the ear, judging fitness as much as skill, where *fluent* asks only that the words come easily.
examples: a few well-spoken words on civic pride

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Idiomatic and comparatively mild - it frames the disagreement as two things standing opposed rather than as either one being wrong.
examples: the figures are at odds with our findings

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Puts the two sides in active collision, stronger than *at odds* but stopping short of claiming they cannot both stand.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The hardest of the disagreement words - it says the two cancel each other, so one of them has to go.
examples: contradictory attributes of unjust justice and loving vindictiveness

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Formal and measuring - it registers the mismatch against the facts coolly, where *incompatible* pronounces on it.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: States the mismatch as a settled property of the thing rather than an observation about it, blunter and more final than *discrepant*.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The plain, unemphatic name for the fault - it marks a failure to hold together without saying how sharp the clash is.
examples: inconsistent statements cannot both be true at the same time

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Informal and slighting - it allows the thing no smooth stretch at all, where *spotty* at least grants good patches between the bad.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Turns the clash inward so no second party is needed - the thing defeats itself, which is the more damning charge.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Informal and deflating - it breaks the thing into good patches and bad ones, so the complaint carries a grudging concession inside it.
examples: the golfer hit the ball well but his putting was spotty

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Technical and unblaming - it records only that two things fail to correspond and leaves the fault unassigned.
examples: a description unconformable to previous accounts

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The mildest of these - it registers variation without deciding that any part of the thing has failed.

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Points at work left undone rather than at a defect - the clash simply stands, not declared unresolvable as *incompatible* would have it.

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Absolute where *destroyed* is elastic - it admits no remnant and no degree, and its sweep makes the ruin sound total rather than merely thorough.

entries.definition: affected by blight; anything that mars or prevents growth or prosperity
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Ruin as a slow affliction rather than an event - what it marks is not smashed but stopped, held back from growing or prospering again.

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Nothingness reached by covering over: the thing is effaced rather than smashed, which makes this the visual member beside the formal *obliterated*.

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Financial ruin in the bluntest available word - a single snap rather than a decline, and it reports the loss without blaming the one it fell on.
examples: the broken fortunes of the family

entries.definition: destroyed or badly damaged by fire
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Says the fire went to its end from the inside and left a hollow behind - more final than plain *burned*, and short of gone.

entries.definition: destroyed or badly damaged by fire
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The particle puts the fire's passage across the thing: it names what the flames swept and left behind them, not what they consumed.
examples: a burned-over site in the forest

entries.definition: destroyed or badly damaged by fire
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Reaches from scorched to gone, fixing fire as the cause while leaving open how much survives - which the compounds beside it refuse to leave open.
examples: a burned-over site in the forest

entries.definition: destroyed or badly damaged by fire
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The clipped twin of *burned-out*, its tighter shape making the hollowness sound like the thing's condition now rather than the fire's doing.
examples: barricaded the street with burnt-out cars

entries.definition: destroyed or badly damaged by fire
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The clipped form, and the shorter shape makes it read as a property the thing now has rather than a report of what happened to it, as *burned* does.
examples: a charred bit of burnt wood
barricaded the street with burnt-out cars

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The elastic member: it stretches from merely spoiled to flattened, so it fixes that ruin happened without fixing how much is left, where *annihilated* leaves nothing to measure.
examples: Alzheimer's is responsible for her destroyed mind

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Carries a purpose *annihilated* does not: the completeness is somebody's work, and the word frames what it names as a thing that was to be got rid of.

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The formal word for that same ruin: it names the poverty left behind rather than the break itself, so it sounds like a settled condition where *broken* sounds like a moment.

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The bare adjectival form states the finished nothingness flatly, without the backward glance at whatever caused it that *obliterated* keeps.

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Formal and cold next to *blotted out*: the participle points back at an act, and what is left is nothing at all rather than something hidden.

entries.definition: affected by blight; anything that mars or prevents growth or prosperity
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: British in spelling and the milder half of its pair: the good has gone out of the thing, where *blighted* adds that nothing will come of it now.

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The informal member, and the offhand phrasing makes the same completeness sound quick and easy rather than momentous beside *annihilated*.
